messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@coauthor.ai>

Cc: Partnerships <partners@coauthor.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CoAuthor SDK bundling / LangChain & LlamaIndex tracing compatibility

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking a look. I’m Samir, head of partnerships at CoAuthor Labs — we build a collaborative writing SDK that surfaces LLM-powered coauthoring flows for product teams. We’ve heard good things about Redwood’s serving runtime and want to explore bundling Redwood as an optional runtime target inside our SDK marketplace.

High-level ask: can we validate (1) compatibility with LangChain and LlamaIndex wrappers we ship, and (2) a lightweight tracing contract so our customers’ prompt/training telemetry flows into their observability (we’d like request-level trace IDs and per-token latency metrics).

Attached is a short proposal and a compatibility matrix we filled out for a first pass. Key items:
- A runtime adapter shim to call Redwood endpoints from our Node + Python SDKs
- A suggested trace envelope (trace_id, request_id, sdk_version, prompt_hash)
- A revenue/packaging conversation (marketplace bundling, co-marketing)

Are you available for a 30-minute tech sync next week? I can bring our lead SDK engineer to walk through the matrix.

Best,
Samir Patel
Head of Partnerships, CoAuthor Labs
attachments: CoAuthor_SDK_Bundling_Proposal_v1.pdf, langchain-compat-matrix.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@coauthor.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CoAuthor SDK bundling / LangChain & LlamaIndex tracing compatibility

Samir — thanks for the clear brief and the matrix. Happy to set up a tech sync. Quick notes before the call so we can be efficient:

- Tracing contract: Redwood supports request-level IDs and token latency breakdowns in the Console and via our trace export API. We prefer a lightweight header (X-Redwood-Trace) that carries trace_id and parent_id; we can map your envelope to ours in the adapter.
- LangChain/LlamaIndex: Our runtime is already compatible with many LangChain adapters but we need to validate the Node/Python wrapper surface you use (especially streaming & function-calling semantics).
- Security: for marketplace bundling we’ll need to confirm whether the integration requires Dedicated or Hosted usage for customers (impacts billing and SSO).

Proposed times: Mon 3/26 10:00-10:30 PT or Tue 3/27 14:00-14:30 PT. Whichever works, please add your SDK lead. I’ll invite Vanessa (partnerships lead) and Marissa (integration PM).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Kimberly — Mon 3/26 10am PT works for us. Lina (cc’d) is our SDK lead and will demo the adapter patterns.

A couple quick clarifications so we can prep:
- On the Dedicated vs Hosted question: our marketplace allows partners to offer both hosted and self-hosted runtime integrations; most early adopters prefer hosted-first. If you have guardrails or contract language for marketplace-hosted bundles, send it over.
- Trace envelope: we can emit X-CoAuthor-Trace and include trace_id/request_id/sdk_version. If you prefer mapping to X-Redwood-Trace on your side, great — let’s align mapping on the call.
- Billing & revenue: we typically discuss a referral split + co-marketing budget. No hard ask here yet — just FYI.

See you Monday.

—Samir

Subject: Fwd: CoAuthor SDK bundling / LangChain & LlamaIndex tracing compatibility — prep + ask list

Folks — forwarding CoAuthor thread. Quick internal prep notes ahead of Monday’s sync (10:00 PT):

Summary: CoAuthor Labs wants to bundle Redwood as a runtime target in their coauthoring SDK marketplace. They care about LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter behavior (streaming + function calls) and a minimalable tracing envelope to capture request/response attribution. They expect hosted-first for early customers and want to discuss revenue/referral later.

My asks for the call:
- Engineering: confirm whether our streaming HTTP semantics and function-calling payload shape are a match for their SDKs. If not, list the compatibility gaps and estimated effort (days).
- Product: what marketplace-hosted guardrails do we need (rate limits, quotas, per-tenant isolation, billing triggers)?
- Legal/RevOps (later): is there a standard partner referral template/discount we can offer?

Notes:
- Attachments included from CoAuthor (proposal + matrix). I put a shared drive folder for artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CoAuthPilot
- Potential win: co-marketing into content creation stacks (Figma, Notion workflows).

Marissa — can you grab the LangChain/LlamaIndex runtime owner (Irene or Jonas) and ask for a 15-min prebrief if there are any red flags?
Vanessa — can you own the partner commercial framing (referral vs revenue share)?

Thanks — see invites.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Partnerships Manager
